ルイ14世・15世の王室礼拝堂楽長。王の食事中に奏でる組曲を書いた。: Master of the Chapel Royal under Louis XIV and Louis XV. He wrote suites to be played while the King dined.
南仏の太陽を、パリの舞台に。: The sun of the Midi, on the stages of Paris.
歌と踊りで、客席を沸かせましょう。: With song and dance, I shall set the house alight.
オペラとバレエを融合した「オペラ・バレ」を確立。南仏エクスの生まれで、陽気なイタ: He established the 'opéra-ballet', fusing opera and ballet. Born in Aix-en-Provence, he brought with him a cheerful Italian taste.
書けば売れる。それが私の流儀でね。: Write it and it sells. That is my way.
楽譜の売り上げ、山分けといこう。: Let us split the takings from the scores.
楽譜の出版で財を成した最初の作曲家のひとり。あまりの多作ぶりを「毎月、苦もなく一: One of the first composers to make a fortune from publishing his music. Teased that he effortlessly 'brought forth a volume every month', he is said to have replied: 'I am earning money.'
もとはバレエの踊り手でね。弓も足さばきが肝心だ。: I began as a ballet dancer, you know. In bowing, too, footwork is everything.
フランス・ヴァイオリン楽派の弓、お貸ししよう。: I shall lend you the bow of the French violin school.
フランス・ヴァイオリン楽派の祖。もとはバレエのダンサーで、1728年にコンセール: Founder of the French violin school. Originally a ballet dancer, he made his debut at the Concert Spirituel in 1728.
今夜は気分が乗らないの。: I am not in the mood tonight.
あなたの舞台なら、すっぽかさないわ。: For your stage, I shall not fail to appear.
パリ・オペラ座の名ソプラノ。気まぐれで、舞台をすっぽかして投獄されたこともある。: A great soprano of the Paris Opéra. Capricious, she was once imprisoned for failing to appear.
6歳のとき、ルイ14世陛下の前で弾いたのですよ。: At the age of six I played before His Majesty Louis XIV.
オルガンの即興なら、お任せを。: For improvisation at the organ, look no further.
神童として名を馳せた鍵盤奏者。1727年、聖ポール教会のオルガニストの座をラモー: A keyboard player famed as a child prodigy. In 1727 he competed with Rameau for the post of organist at Saint-Paul and won.
マレ「膀胱結石手術図」: Marais: 'Le Tableau de l'opération de la taille'
ドラランド『王の晩餐のためのサンフォニー』: Delalande: Symphonies pour les Soupers du Roy
王妃さまが、私の新作を待っておられるのです。: The Queen is waiting for my new work.
オペラ・コミックの笑いと涙を、あなたの舞台に。: The laughter and tears of opéra-comique, for your stage.
ベルギー出身のオペラ・コミックの王。王妃マリー・アントワネットのお気に入りだった: The Belgian-born king of opéra-comique. A favourite of Queen Marie Antoinette.
フランスにも交響曲はあるのですよ。: France has symphonies too, you know.
楽団の束ね役、お引き受けしよう。: I shall take on the task of holding the orchestra together.
「フランス交響曲の父」。コンセール・デ・ザマトゥールを創設し、のちにサン＝ジョル: 'Father of the French symphony'. He founded the Concert des Amateurs and later handed its direction to Saint-Georges.
チェス盤と五線譜、どちらも同じさ。: The chessboard and the stave are one and the same.
次の一手は、あなたと組むことだ。: My next move is to join you.
作曲家にして当代最強のチェス指し。目隠しで3人同時に対局してロンドン中を驚かせた: A composer and the strongest chess player of his day. He astonished London by playing three games at once blindfold. His Analyse du jeu des Échecs is regarded as a classic.
悲劇の女王なら、私の右に出る者はいないわ。: For tragic queens, no one surpasses me.
あなたの舞台で、パリを泣かせましょう。: On your stage, I shall make Paris weep.
パリ・オペラ座の悲劇女優型ソプラノ。ピッチンニ『ディドン』（1783）で大当たり: A soprano of the tragic-actress type at the Paris Opéra. She had a great triumph in Piccinni's Didon (1783).
チェロの指使いを、一から考え直しているところだ。: I am rethinking cello fingering from the very beginning.
近代チェロの奏法、お見せしよう。: Let me show you the modern way of playing the cello.
チェロの近代的な運指法を確立した名手。のちにナポレオンが彼のストラディヴァリを借: The virtuoso who established modern cello fingering. Napoleon is said later to have borrowed his Stradivari to try it and scratched it with the spur of his boot.
フルートもファゴットも、両方吹けますよ。: Flute or bassoon — I play both.
フルートとファゴットの名手で「フランスのモーツァルト」と呼ばれた。: A virtuoso of both flute and bassoon, called 'the French Mozart'.
私のオペラで、革命が起きたこともあるのですよ。: An opera of mine once started a revolution, you know.
劇場を沸かせる術なら、心得ています。: I know the art of setting a theatre alight.
1830年、ブリュッセルでの『ポルティチの唖娘』上演中に観客が蜂起し、ベルギー独: In 1830, during a performance of La Muette de Portici in Brussels, the audience rose in revolt: the spark of the Belgian Revolution.
音楽院の授業がありましてね。: I have my classes at the Conservatoire, you see.
教え子たちごと、力を貸しましょう。: I shall lend you my strength, pupils and all.
パリ音楽院の教授で、グノーやビゼーを育てた。ビゼーはのちに彼の娘と結婚した。: Professor at the Paris Conservatoire, teacher of Gounod and Bizet. Bizet later married his daughter.
バレエなら、ひと月で書き上げますよ。: A ballet? I can write one in a month.
踊れる音楽を、お約束しましょう。: I promise you music one can dance to.
バレエ『ジゼル』（1841）や、クリスマス聖歌「さやかに星はきらめき」の作曲者。: Composer of the ballet Giselle (1841) and of the Christmas carol 'Minuit, chrétiens' (O Holy Night).
短調による12の練習曲: Twelve Études in the minor keys
人前に出るのは、あまり好きではないのです。: I am not fond of appearing in public.
ショパンの友人なら、信用しましょう。: A friend of Chopin's I can trust.
リストも一目置いた超絶技巧のピアニスト。極端な人嫌いで長く隠遁した。ショパンとは: A pianist of transcendent technique whom even Liszt respected. Extremely unsociable, he lived long as a recluse. He was Chopin's neighbour and close friend.
男性教授と同じ給料。それが私の条件です。: The same salary as the male professors. That is my condition.
19世紀のパリ音楽院で、ただ一人の女性の正教授（ピアノ科、1842年から30年）: The only woman to hold a full professorship at the Paris Conservatoire in the 19th century (piano, for 30 years from 1842). She fought for the same salary as her male colleagues and won it after the success of her Nonet.
舞台にガス灯を入れたら、尼僧の亡霊が踊り出しましてね。: We put gaslight on the stage — and the ghosts of nuns began to dance.
グランド・オペラの物量で、圧倒しましょう。: Let us overwhelm them with the sheer scale of grand opera.
パリ・オペラ座のグランド・オペラの帝王。『悪魔のロベール』の「尼僧たちのバレエ」: Emperor of grand opera at the Paris Opéra. The 'Ballet of the Nuns' in Robert le diable caused a sensation.
ナポレオン陛下の前でも吹いたのですよ。: I have played before His Majesty Napoleon himself.
ナポレオンのお抱えフルート奏者として名を上げた名手。: A virtuoso who made his name as Napoleon's personal flautist.
マリアのそばにいられるなら、どこへでも。: Wherever I can be near Maria.
ベルギーのヴァイオリンの名手。歌姫マリブランの恋人で、のちに夫となった。: A Belgian violin virtuoso. Lover of the diva Malibran, and later her husband.
サント・クロチルドのオルガンが待っているのでね。: The organ of Sainte-Clotilde is waiting for me.
神の御心のままに、力を貸そう。: As God wills, I shall lend my strength.
サント・クロチルド教会のオルガニスト。代表作の多くは60歳を過ぎてから書かれた。: Organist of Sainte-Clotilde. Most of his major works were written after the age of 60. The Violin Sonata was a wedding present for Ysaÿe.
サラサーテ君のために書いた曲がありましてね。: I have a piece I wrote for young Sarasate.
スペインの情熱を、あなたの楽団に。: The passion of Spain, for your orchestra.
『スペイン交響曲』（1875）はサラサーテのために書かれた。もとは弦楽四重奏のヴ: The Symphonie espagnole (1875) was written for Sarasate. He began as the violist of a string quartet.
新しいオペラ座で、バレエを初演したばかりです。: I have just given a ballet its premiere at the new Opéra.
踊る音楽なら、お任せを。: Music for dancing? Leave it to me.
『コッペリア』と『シルヴィア』でバレエ音楽を一新した。チャイコフスキーは『シルヴ: With Coppélia and Sylvia he transformed ballet music. Tchaikovsky wrote that after hearing Sylvia he was ashamed of his own Swan Lake.
神々もカンカンを踊る時代ですよ。: These are days when even the gods dance the cancan.
笑いと儲けは、私にお任せを。: Laughter and profit — leave both to me.
オペレッタの王。1876年にはアメリカ巡業を行った。ドイツ生まれのチェロの名手で: King of operetta. In 1876 he toured America. German-born, he was also a cello virtuoso.
ロンドンから戻ったばかりでね。: I am only just back from London.
祈りのような旋律を、あなたの舞台に。: Melodies like prayers, for your stage.
『ファウスト』（1859）は当時もっとも上演されたオペラのひとつ。バッハの前奏曲: Faust (1859) was one of the most performed operas of its time. He is also known for the 'Ave Maria' that lays a melody over a Bach prelude.
甘い旋律は、罪でしょうか。: Is a sweet melody a sin?
パリの客をとろかせましょう。: Let us melt the hearts of Paris.
甘美な旋律でオペラ界を席巻した。パリ音楽院でシャルパンティエらを教えた。: He swept the opera world with his sweet melodies. At the Paris Conservatoire he taught Charpentier among others.
マドレーヌ寺院の聖歌隊の練習がありまして。: I have choir practice at the Madeleine.
マドレーヌ寺院で師サン＝サーンスの代役を務め、1877年に聖歌隊長となった。ヴァ: He deputised at the Madeleine for his teacher Saint-Saëns and became choirmaster there in 1877. The First Violin Sonata was completed in 1876 and first performed the following year. He and Saint-Saëns were friends for life.
今夜も私のサロンへいらして。: Do come to my salon again tonight.
歌でも人脈でも、お力になりますわ。: With my voice or my connections, I shall help you.
マリブランの妹。歌手・作曲家・サロンの女主人としてパリの楽壇を支えた。ツルゲーネ: Malibran's sister. As singer, composer and salon hostess she was a pillar of musical Paris. The woman Turgenev loved all his life.
サン・シュルピスのオルガン、聴きにいらっしゃい。: Come and hear the organ of Saint-Sulpice.
オルガンの大伽藍を、あなたの楽団に。: The cathedral of the organ, for your orchestra.
1870年から64年間、サン・シュルピス教会のオルガニストを務めた。: Organist of Saint-Sulpice for 64 years from 1870.
オッフェンバック『天国と地獄』のカンカン: The cancan from Offenbach's Orphée aux enfers
サン＝サーンス『動物の謝肉祭』「白鳥」: Saint-Saëns: 'Le Cygne' from Le Carnaval des animaux
私の音楽は、家具のように聞き流してくれればいい。: My music may be ignored like the furniture.
面白い。ただし、傘は持っていくよ。: Interesting. But I shall bring my umbrella.
モンマルトルのキャバレーのピアニスト。1905年、39歳でスコラ・カントルムに入: A cabaret pianist in Montmartre. In 1905, at 39, he went back to school at the Schola Cantorum. He proposed 'furniture music'.
『フランスの山人の歌による交響曲』: Symphonie sur un chant montagnard français
スコラ・カントルムの授業があるのでね。: I have classes at the Schola Cantorum.
フランク先生の教えにかけて。: On the teaching of Maître Franck.
スコラ・カントルムの創設者。フランクの高弟で、サティやルーセルを教えた。: Founder of the Schola Cantorum. A leading pupil of Franck, he taught Satie and Roussel.
完璧でない曲は、燃やしてしまうのです。: A piece that is not perfect, I burn.
完璧な一曲を、お約束しよう。: I promise you one perfect piece.
極端な完璧主義者で、晩年に多くの作品を自ら破棄した。『魔法使いの弟子』はのちにデ: An extreme perfectionist who destroyed many of his own works late in life. L'Apprenti sorcier later became widely known through a Disney film.
規律なくして、自由はありません。: Without discipline there is no freedom.
教え子たちごと、楽団を鍛えましょう。: With my pupils, I shall train your orchestra.
1908年のローマ賞で、声楽フーガの課題に器楽フーガを出して物議を醸した。のちに: At the 1908 Prix de Rome she caused a stir by submitting an instrumental fugue for the vocal fugue set. She later became the greatest composition teacher of the 20th century.
姉が、あなたの楽団を褒めていました。: My sister spoke well of your orchestra.
書けるうちに、書いておきたいのです。: I want to write while I still can.
1913年、女性として初めてローマ賞の大賞を受賞した。姉ナディアの教え子。幼い頃: In 1913 she became the first woman to win the Prix de Rome grand prize. A pupil of her sister Nadia. Frail from childhood.
メリザンドを歌えるのは、私だけよ。: I am the only one who can sing Mélisande.
パリでもシカゴでも、満員にしてみせるわ。: Paris or Chicago, I shall fill the house.
スコットランド出身。1902年、『ペレアスとメリザンド』の初演でメリザンドを創唱: Born in Scotland. In 1902 she created the role of Mélisande at the premiere of Pelléas et Mélisande.
ストラヴィンスキー『春の祭典』初演: Premiere of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring
どんなに客席が荒れても、最後まで振りますよ。: However wild the house becomes, I conduct to the end.
冷静なタクトを、お貸ししよう。: Let me lend you a cool baton.
バレエ・リュスの指揮者。1913年、怒号と乱闘の中で『春の祭典』の初演を最後まで: Conductor of the Ballets Russes. In 1913 he conducted the premiere of The Rite of Spring through to the end amid shouting and brawling. Originally a violist.
フォーレ先生の音楽は、私が守ります。: Maître Fauré's music is in my keeping.
フランスのピアノを、あなたの楽団に。: The French piano, for your orchestra.
フォーレとラヴェルの名解釈者。のちにラヴェルのピアノ協奏曲ト長調を初演した。: A great interpreter of Fauré and Ravel. She later gave the premiere of Ravel's Piano Concerto in G.
ファゴット代わりのクラリネット: Clarinet in place of the bassoon

革命を起こしたオペラ: The opera that started a revolution

マラン・マレがパリで世を去った。ヴィオールの時代の終わりを告げる死だった。: Marin Marais has died in Paris. His death marks the end of the age of the viol.
オルガニスト選考の因縁: The grudge of the organist contest
スコラ・カントルムの師弟: Master and pupil of the Schola Cantorum

史実のパガニーニは、カジノ・パガニーニの失敗で財産の多くを失い、1840年にニー: The real Paganini lost much of his fortune in the failure of the Casino Paganini and died in Nice in 1840.
史実のリストは1847年に演奏活動から退き、ワイマールで指揮と作曲に専念した。晩: The real Liszt retired from the concert platform in 1847 and devoted himself to conducting and composing in Weimar. Late in life he took minor orders.
史実のモーツァルトは1791年、35歳でウィーンに没した。借金を抱えたまま、共同: The real Mozart died in Vienna in 1791, aged 35. Still in debt, he was buried in a common grave.
史実のワーグナーは1883年にヴェネツィアで没した。バイロイト音楽祭は今も毎夏開: The real Wagner died in Venice in 1883. The Bayreuth Festival is still held every summer.
史実のブラームスは1897年にウィーンで没した。最後まで独身を通し、クララ・シュ: The real Brahms died in Vienna in 1897, a bachelor to the last, the year after the death of Clara Schumann.
史実のバッハは1750年にライプツィヒで没し、その音楽は一時忘れられた。1829: The real Bach died in Leipzig in 1750, and for a time his music was forgotten. It came back to life in 1829, with Mendelssohn's revival of the St Matthew Passion.
史実のヘンデルはオペラ興行で破産しかけたが、英語のオラトリオ『メサイア』で復活し: The real Handel was nearly ruined by his opera ventures, but rose again with the English oratorio Messiah and was buried in Westminster Abbey.
史実のマーラーは1911年に没した。「いずれ私の時代が来る」の言葉どおり、約半世: The real Mahler died in 1911. True to his words 'My time will come', a worldwide Mahler boom arrived about half a century later.
史実のR.シュトラウスは1949年まで生き、最晩年に『4つの最後の歌』を遺した。: The real R. Strauss lived until 1949 and left the Four Last Songs at the very end of his life.
楽団の譜面はやがて書庫に眠ったが、およそ100年後、ある若き指揮者がその写譜を見: The orchestra's parts came to rest in an archive, but some 100 years later a young conductor would find the copies and astonish the world.
後世の音楽史家は、ウィーン古典派の黄金時代はこの楽団から始まったと書いている。: Later historians of music write that the golden age of Viennese Classicism began with this orchestra.
その後、楽団はヨーロッパ各地を巡業し、「ロマン派の旅する大楽団」と呼ばれた。: Afterwards the orchestra toured all over Europe and was called 'the great travelling orchestra of the Romantics'.
「音楽戦争」を制した楽団は、世紀末へ向かう楽壇の中心に立ち続けた。: Having won the 'War of the Romantics', the orchestra stayed at the centre of the musical world as the century drew to its close.
大戦の足音が迫るなか、楽団は大西洋を渡り、新大陸で新しい時代の響きを築いた。: As the footsteps of the Great War drew near, the orchestra crossed the Atlantic and built the sound of a new age in the New World.

How to play
  1. Tap a city on the map to travel. Persuade the musicians in each city to join your orchestra.
  2. A persuasion lasts 8 bars. Use Fee, Scandal, Theory, Fame and Passion as the moment requires; push the rapport needle all the way to the right and they are won over. Different approaches work on different people (and repeating one weakens it).
  3. When inspiration is full, a cadenza gives a big push. Attend a salon beforehand and you start with inspiration already stored.
  4. If talks break down, you can convince them in a performance duel: Technique, Expression and Improvisation, like rock-paper-scissors.
  5. Persuade the ruler of a city (a theatre or a court) and the city is yours, with an income every month.
  6. Every month the rival camps poach musicians, seize cities and launch concert wars against your cities. Win back their cities by concert war and their followers by poaching.
  7. Those far above you (Lv more than your fame Lv+2) will turn you away. Give concerts to raise your fame.
  8. Choose a venue: salon, medium hall or large theatre. Bigger earns more but empties more easily. The audience's reaction (bravos, bouquets, swoons, boos, dozing, walk-outs) depends on the reception.
  9. Each player has a ★trait (attendance +20%, strings +3, lesson income…) and a quirk (frail, miser, difficult, amorous…). When satisfaction falls they may leave, or go over to a rival. A friend already in your orchestra will put in a word during persuasion.
  10. Scouting: first 🔍scout (150 fr) to learn which approaches work, the growth type (early / normal / late), potential, contract terms and chemistry. Without scouting you cannot tell which approach worked. Once they are won over, negotiate the signing fee and salary (haggling is a gamble).
  11. Ensemble and chemistry: the more two players appear together, the higher their ensemble Lv and the better the reception. Pairs with ◎○ chemistry grow quickly; ✕ pairs drag each other down and lose satisfaction.
  12. Growth types: early bloomers grow fast at first but decline from the fifth year; late bloomers grow strongly after two and a half years.
  13. Meet the victory conditions and you face the final showdown (best of three). Win it and the grand concert follows.
  14. At a concert you choose the programme and place your players in each part, like a football formation. The abilities the piece calls for, form (which changes monthly), historical partnerships (chemistry), the composer's presence and the city's taste decide the reception (★).
  15. In a performance duel, taking a player as your second strengthens that person's best card.
  16. There are five difficulty levels: Beginner, Normal, Hard, Very hard, Inferno. The victory conditions (cities held and seats filled) and the time limit vary with difficulty. The more cities you hold, the more wary the remaining theatres and courts become, and their rank rises.
  17. Fame tops out at Lv30. After clearing the game you can go on without a time limit in endless mode and collect 🏅achievements.

ブダペストの名教授。ヨアヒムに学び、のちのハンガリー・ヴァイオリン楽派を育てた。: A celebrated professor in Budapest. He studied with Joachim and raised the later Hungarian violin school.
ブラームス先生に、ほめていただいたことがあります。: Herr Brahms once had kind words for me.
ハンガリーの鍵盤を、あなたの楽団に。: The Hungarian keyboard, for your orchestra.
ハンガリーの名ピアニスト・作曲家。若くしてブラームスに作品を認められ、バルトーク: A fine Hungarian pianist and composer. Brahms recognised his work when he was young, and he made his name before Bartók.
蓄音機を担いで、村をまわっています。: I go round the villages with a phonograph on my back.
民の歌を、あなたの楽団に。: The songs of the people, for your orchestra.
1905年に農村で民謡を集め始め、翌年からはバルトークとともに蓄音機を持って村々: He began collecting folk songs in the countryside in 1905, and from the next year toured the villages with Bartók, carrying a phonograph.
ヴァイオリンもピアノも、どちらも本業です。: Violin and piano — both are my profession.
ルーマニアの魂を、あなたの楽団に。: The soul of Romania, for your orchestra.
ルーマニア出身。ヴァイオリン・ピアノ・作曲のすべてに秀でた天才で、のちにメニュー: Born in Romania. A genius who excelled as violinist, pianist and composer alike; he later taught Menuhin.
チェルノホルスキーがグラーツで世を去った。「ボヘミアのバッハ」の死だった。: Černohorský has died in Graz: the passing of 'the Bohemian Bach'.
F.X.ドゥシェクがプラハで世を去った。: F.X. Dušek has died in Prague.
ジョン・フィールドがモスクワで世を去った。夜想曲の父の死だった。: John Field has died in Moscow: the passing of the father of the nocturne.
ムソルグスキーがペテルブルクで世を去った。42歳だった。: Mussorgsky has died in St Petersburg, aged 42.
N.ルビンシテインがパリで世を去った。チャイコフスキーは彼の死を悼んでピアノ三重: N. Rubinstein has died in Paris. Tchaikovsky wrote his Piano Trio in his memory.
ボロディンが舞踏会の最中に倒れ、世を去った。歌劇『イーゴリ公』は未完のまま残され: Borodin collapsed and died in the middle of a ball. His opera Prince Igor was left unfinished.
リムスキー＝コルサコフが世を去った。歌劇『金鶏』の初演を見ることはなかった。: Rimsky-Korsakov has died. He never saw the premiere of his opera The Golden Cockerel.
カルウォヴィチがタトラ山脈で雪崩に遭い、世を去った。32歳だった。: Karłowicz has died in an avalanche in the Tatras, aged 32.
拍子取りの巻紙（ロール）: Roll of paper for beating time
モスクワ音楽院の師弟: Masters and pupils of the Moscow Conservatory
弦楽四重奏の地方巡業: A provincial tour for string quartet
ペテルブルク宮廷への長期招聘: A long engagement at the St Petersburg court
渾身のタクト: A baton with everything behind it
新作の主題: The theme of a new work
ハイドンはモーツァルトの父に「ご子息は最大の作曲家」と語り、若きベートーヴェンは: Haydn told Mozart's father that his son was 'the greatest composer', and the young Beethoven studied with Haydn.
ショパンとリストは1830年代のパリで互いの演奏会に立ち、フランコムはショパン最: In the Paris of the 1830s Chopin and Liszt appeared at each other's concerts, and Franchomme was Chopin's finest chamber-music partner.
1853年、20歳のブラームスがシューマン家の扉を叩いた。ローベルトは評論で彼を: In 1853 the 20-year-old Brahms knocked at the Schumanns' door. Robert introduced him to the world in an article.
ベッリーニの『夢遊病の女』はパスタのために、マリブランはその役で一世を風靡した。: Bellini's La sonnambula was written for Pasta, and Malibran took the age by storm in the role.
1876年、第1回バイロイト音楽祭。『指環』初演の指揮台にはハンス・リヒターが立: 1876, the first Bayreuth Festival. Hans Richter stood on the podium for the premiere of the Ring.
セネジーノとクッツォーニ、そしてファウスティーナ。ロンドンのイタリア・オペラは歌: Senesino, Cuzzoni, and then Faustina. Italian opera in London blazed with the sparks its singers struck.
ピゼンデルが率いたドレスデン宮廷楽団は、当時ヨーロッパ随一とうたわれた。: The Dresden court orchestra led by Pisendel was praised as the finest in Europe in its day.
マンハイムの楽団を、ある英国人は「将軍たちの軍隊」と評した。: An Englishman called the Mannheim orchestra 'an army of generals'.
チャイコフスキーからラフマニノフへ。ロシアの旋律が西欧の舞台を席巻した。: From Tchaikovsky to Rachmaninoff: Russian melody swept the stages of western Europe.
国民音楽協会のもと、フランスの作曲家たちはドイツとは違う響きを求めた。: Under the Société nationale de musique, French composers sought a sound different from Germany's.
ワルターはマーラーの弟子で右腕。シェーンベルクの才能を真っ先に認めたのもマーラー: Walter was Mahler's pupil and right hand. It was Mahler, too, who first recognised Schoenberg's gift.
ルイ14世以来の宮廷音楽。クープランとマレの響きは、王の権威そのものだった。: Court music since Louis XIV. The sound of Couperin and Marais was the very authority of the King.
フランクのオルガン教室からダンディやデュカスが巣立ち、フランス音楽の背骨をつくっ: From Franck's organ class came d'Indy and Dukas, who formed the backbone of French music.
独学の作曲家たちが集まり、西欧の作法にとらわれないロシアの音楽をつくろうとした。: Self-taught composers came together to make a Russian music free of western European conventions.
ルビンシテインが創り、チャイコフスキーが教え、タネーエフからラフマニノフとスクリ: Founded by Rubinstein, taught by Tchaikovsky, and on from Taneyev to Rachmaninoff and Scriabin.
A.ルビンシテインが1862年に創った、ロシア最初の音楽院。: Russia's first conservatory, founded by A. Rubinstein in 1862.
「ヨーロッパの音楽学校」と呼ばれたボヘミアは、各地の宮廷に名手を送り出した。: Bohemia, called 'the conservatory of Europe', sent virtuosos to courts everywhere.
リストからエルケル、フバイ、そしてバルトークとコダーイへ。ハンガリーの響きは受け: From Liszt to Erkel and Hubay, and on to Bartók and Kodály: the Hungarian sound was handed down.
エルスネルに学び、クルピンスキの棒で弾いた若きショパンは、20歳でワルシャワを去: The young Chopin studied with Elsner, played under Kurpiński's baton, and left Warsaw at 20.
本来なら出会うはずのない音楽家どうしが、同じ舞台で音を重ねる。: Musicians who could never have met share a stage and join their sound.
クレモナのアマティ一族はヴァイオリン製作の祖。のちの名工たちもその流れをくむ。: The Amati family of Cremona were the founders of violin making. The great makers who followed descend from them.
1716年製。ほとんど弾かれないまま保存され、今も新品同様の姿を伝える。: Made in 1716. Preserved almost unplayed, it still looks like new.
パガニーニの愛器。轟く音から「大砲」と呼ばれ、遺言で故郷ジェノヴァに遺された。: Paganini's own instrument. Called 'the Cannon' for its thunderous sound, it was left by his will to his native Genoa.
ヴェネツィアの名工ゴフリラー。チェロの名器で知られる。: Goffriller, the Venetian master, is known for his superb cellos.
1712年製。ロシアの名手ダヴィドフが弾き、のちにデュ・プレの愛器となった。: Made in 1712. Played by the Russian virtuoso Davidov, and later the instrument of du Pré.
16世紀ブレシアの名工の作。コントラバスの名手ドラゴネッティが愛用した。: The work of a 16th-century master of Brescia. The double-bass virtuoso Dragonetti played one.
アントワープのリュッカース一族のチェンバロは、改造してでも使い続けられた名器。: Harpsichords by the Ruckers family of Antwerp were so prized that they were rebuilt to keep them in use.
ザクセンのジルバーマンはオルガンと鍵盤楽器の名工。バッハとも交流があった。: Silbermann of Saxony was a master builder of organs and keyboard instruments. He and Bach knew each other.
アウクスブルクのシュタイン。1777年、モーツァルトがその鍵盤を手紙で絶賛した。: Stein of Augsburg. In 1777 Mozart praised his keyboards to the skies in a letter.
エラール社のダブル・エスケープメントで、速い同音連打が可能になった。: Érard's double escapement made rapid repeated notes possible.
ショパンは調子のよい日にはプレイエルを選んだと伝わる。: Chopin is said to have chosen a Pleyel on days when he felt well.
1884年に登場したスタインウェイのフルコンサート・グランド。: Steinway's full concert grand, which appeared in 1884.
クヴァンツはフリードリヒ大王のフルートの師。自ら楽器も設計した。: Quantz was flute teacher to Frederick the Great. He designed instruments himself.
ベームが1847年に完成させた円筒管のフルート。今日のフルートの原型。: The cylindrical flute Boehm perfected in 1847: the prototype of today's flute.
クラリネットの前身。ニュルンベルクのデンナーが改良したとされる。: Forerunner of the clarinet. Denner of Nuremberg is credited with improving it.
モーツァルトのクラリネット協奏曲は、シュタードラーのこの楽器のために書かれた。: Mozart's Clarinet Concerto was written for this instrument of Stadler's.
20世紀初めにエーラーが完成させたドイツ式クラリネット。: The German-system clarinet perfected by Oehler in the early 20th century.
メンデルスゾーンはゲヴァントハウスで細い指揮棒を振ったとされる。: Mendelssohn is said to have conducted at the Gewandhaus with a slender baton.
19世紀、象牙の指揮棒は名指揮者への名誉の贈り物でもあった。: In the 19th century an ivory baton was also a gift of honour to a great conductor.
昔は巻いた紙や杖で拍を取った。リュリは杖で足を突き、それがもとで亡くなった。: Time was once beaten with a roll of paper or a staff. Lully struck his foot with his staff, and died of it.
多くの名作は、この一本のペンから生まれた。: Many a masterpiece came from this one pen.
初版の楽譜には、作曲者自身の意図がいちばん色濃く残る。: A first edition keeps the composer's own intentions most vividly.
1815年にメルツェルが特許を取った。ベートーヴェンは早くから速度表示に使った。: Patented by Maelzel in 1815. Beethoven was quick to use it for tempo markings.
円盤式の蓄音機。カルーソーの録音で一気に広まった。: The disc gramophone. Caruso's recordings made it spread at a stroke.
弓の毛に塗る樹脂。良い松脂は音の立ち上がりを変える。: The resin rubbed on the bow hair. Good rosin changes the attack of the sound.
歌手の喉を守る昔ながらの知恵。: An old piece of wisdom for protecting a singer's throat.
オペラの舞台は衣装でも競われた。: On the operatic stage, costumes too were a field of rivalry.
演奏会の正装。: Formal dress for the concert platform.
18世紀の宮廷では、鬘なしで人前に出ることはなかった。: At 18th-century courts no one appeared in public without a wig.

Travel, persuasion, duels and concerts are as before. Added to them are tours on which you train and lead your orchestra.
Rehearsal room
Choose up to six for the touring party (you may be one of them). The first is the concertmaster. Players grow from Lv1 to 99 and at Lv20 can be awakened (abilities and trait grow). Give each up to two belongings — instruments or tools (only ones that exist in that era). Gather companions from history and a historical tie is formed.
Tours
You play the venues of the city you are in, one night at a time. Each night you look at the audience and choose a playing style; the performance runs overture → first movement → second movement → encore. On the road between venues, things happen. Each ovation on the grand master's stage crumbles the stronghold; at 0 the city is yours. Musicians you meet may ask to join. Force a player at the limit on stage and they will leave the orchestra.
Engagements
Send the engagement party out on a job lasting some months to earn funds.
Door of Time
Opens once you hold 3 cities. Conquer it for an 'Invitation across Time', with which you can invite a musician of another era (Bach, Mahler and others) as a guest.
左手は、まだ誰も行ったことのない高さまで届きますよ。: My left hand reaches heights no one has yet visited.
あなたの楽団で、ローマ仕込みの技を。: Skills schooled in Rome, in your orchestra.
ローマで修業した名手。協奏曲に付けた24のカプリースは、のちのパガニーニの先駆け: A virtuoso trained in Rome. The 24 caprices attached to his concertos foreshadowed Paganini.
窓から飛び降りたのは、ちょっとした行き違いでしてね。: Jumping from the window was a small misunderstanding, you see.
わたしほどの名手は、ヨーロッパに二人といませんよ。: There are not two virtuosos like me in Europe.
傲慢で知られた天才。1722年、ドレスデンで同僚と揉めたあと窓から飛び降り、足を: A genius known for his arrogance. In 1722, after a dispute with a colleague in Dresden, he leapt from a window and hurt his leg. Afterwards he found refuge in Prague.
ピエタの格子の向こうで、ずっと弾いてきました。: I have always played behind the grille of the Pietà.
一度でいいから、格子の外で弾いてみたい。: Just once, I should like to play outside the grille.
ヴェネツィアのピエタ慈善院で育った孤児の名手。ヴィヴァルディは彼女のために多くの: An orphan raised at the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice who became a virtuoso. Vivaldi wrote many concertos for her.
ピゼンデル先生に習っています。: I am studying with Herr Pisendel.
いつか、あなたの楽団のコンマスに。: One day, concertmaster of your orchestra.
ドレスデンでピゼンデルに学んだ若者。のちにプロイセンのフリードリヒ皇太子の楽団で: A young man who studied with Pisendel in Dresden. He would later be concertmaster of the orchestra of Crown Prince Frederick of Prussia.
コンセール・スピリチュエルは、わたしの庭のようなものです。: The Concert Spirituel is as good as my own garden.
フランスのヴァイオリンを、あなたの楽団に。: The French violin, for your orchestra.
ヴィオッティが「フランスのタルティーニ」と呼んだ名手。のちにパリ音楽院の最初のヴ: A virtuoso whom Viotti called 'the French Tartini'. He later became the first professor of violin at the Paris Conservatoire.
練習曲なら、いくらでも書けますよ。: Études? I can write as many as you like.
パリの若手の弓を、あなたの楽団に。: The bow of young Paris, for your orchestra.
パリの若きヴァイオリニスト。のちにベートーヴェンからソナタを献呈されたが、一度も: A young violinist of Paris. Beethoven later dedicated a sonata to him, which he is said never once to have played.
アダージョ？ わたしの国では、ゆっくり弾く者はいませんよ。: Adagio? In my country nobody plays slowly.
女帝陛下にも負けない給金を、お約束いただけるなら。: If you can promise me pay to match Her Majesty the Empress's.
エカチェリーナ2世の宮廷に仕えた奇抜な名手。速いパッセージは無類だが、ゆっくりし: An eccentric virtuoso at the court of Catherine II. Peerless in fast passages, he is said to have been poor in slow music.
モーツァルトさんの楽譜は、いつも直前に届くのです。: Herr Mozart's music always arrives at the last minute.
あなたの楽団で、歌うように弾きましょう。: In your orchestra I shall play as if singing.
女性の名ヴァイオリニスト。1784年、モーツァルトが彼女のためにソナタK.454: A celebrated woman violinist. In 1784 Mozart wrote the Sonata K. 454 for her and played the concert with his own part still a blank page.
ロンドンの楽団は、わたしが率いております。: I lead the orchestras of London.
ロンドン仕込みのリーダーシップを、あなたの楽団に。: Leadership schooled in London, for your orchestra.
マンハイム出身でロンドンの楽団を率いた名リーダー。改良した「クラーマー型」の弓は: Born in Mannheim, a great leader of London orchestras. His improved 'Cramer' bow was ahead of its time.
マンハイムの弓さばきは、揃うことが命です。: In Mannheim bowing, unanimity is everything.
あなたの楽団の弦を、揃えてみせましょう。: I shall bring the strings of your orchestra together.
マンハイム楽派のヴァイオリニスト。宮廷とともにミュンヘンへ移った。: A violinist of the Mannheim school. He moved to Munich with the court.
ヴァイオリン協奏曲 第8番「劇唱の形式で」: Violin Concerto No. 8 'in modo di scena cantante'
ドイツの正統なヴァイオリンを、あなたの楽団に。: The true German violin, for your orchestra.
カッセルの宮廷楽長で、ドイツ随一のヴァイオリニスト。顎当てを考案し、指揮棒を最初: Court Kapellmeister in Kassel and Germany's foremost violinist. He invented the chin rest and is counted among the first to use a baton.
メンデルスゾーン君とは、子どものころからの友人です。: Mendelssohn and I have been friends since childhood.
のちにゲヴァントハウスのコンサートマスターとなり、メンデルスゾーンの協奏曲を助言: Later concertmaster of the Gewandhaus; he advised on Mendelssohn's concerto and gave its premiere.
ノルウェーの滝の音を、そのままヴァイオリンに。: The sound of Norway's waterfalls, straight onto the violin.
北の国の弓を、あなたの楽団に。: The bow of the North, for your orchestra.
ノルウェーの独学の名手。1831年にパリへ出てパガニーニを聴いて奮起し、のちに「: A self-taught Norwegian virtuoso. He went to Paris in 1831, was fired up by hearing Paganini, and was later called 'the Paganini of the North'.
ウィーンを出たことは、ほとんどありません。: I have scarcely ever left Vienna.
ウィーンの甘い音色を、あなたの楽団に。: The sweet tone of Vienna, for your orchestra.
ウィーン宮廷の名ヴァイオリニスト。華麗な作風で、ウィーンでは絶大な人気があった。: A celebrated violinist of the Viennese court. His brilliant style made him enormously popular in Vienna.
パガニーニ先生の、ただ一人の弟子です。: I am Maestro Paganini's one and only pupil.
先生ゆずりの技を、あなたの楽団に。: My master's art, for your orchestra.
パガニーニが生涯でただ一人とった弟子。師から、愛器「イル・カノーネ」をヴィヨーム: The only pupil Paganini ever took. His master gave him a fine copy of 'Il Cannone', his own violin, made by Vuillaume.
ド・ベリオ先生に、よくほめられます。: Monsieur de Bériot often praises me.
ぼく、もっと大きな舞台で弾きたいんです。: I want to play on bigger stages.
ベルギーの神童。ド・ベリオに学び、まだ十代で各地を巡演していた。のちにフランコ＝: A Belgian prodigy. A pupil of de Bériot, he was touring while still in his teens. He would become a great master of the Franco-Belgian school.
ロンドンの次は、ブリュッセルの生徒たちが待っています。: After London, my students in Brussels are waiting.
ポーランドの弓を、あなたの楽団に。: The Polish bow, for your orchestra.
ポーランドの大ヴァイオリニスト。ロシア宮廷のソリストを経てブリュッセル音楽院の教: A great Polish violinist. After serving as soloist to the Russian court he became a professor at the Brussels Conservatoire.
女がヴァイオリンを弾くなんて、と言われたものです。: 'A woman, playing the violin!' they used to say.
あなたの楽団の舞台に立ちましょう。: I shall take the stage with your orchestra.
モラヴィア出身の女性ヴァイオリニスト。ロンドンで絶大な人気を誇り、のちにハレ夫人: A woman violinist from Moravia. Hugely popular in London, she later became Lady Hallé.
バイロイトの楽団は、わたしが率いています。: I lead the orchestra at Bayreuth.
祝祭劇場のコンマスを、あなたの楽団に。: The concertmaster of the Festspielhaus, for your orchestra.
1876年の第1回バイロイト音楽祭でコンサートマスターを務めた。バッハのアリアを: Concertmaster at the first Bayreuth Festival in 1876. He arranged Bach's air and made it famous as the 'Air on the G String'.
チャイコフスキーさんの協奏曲、誰も弾かないならわたしが。: If no one will play Tchaikovsky's concerto, I will.
あなたの楽団で、新しい協奏曲を。: A new concerto, with your orchestra.
モスクワ音楽院の教授。のちに「演奏不可能」と言われたチャイコフスキーの協奏曲を初: Professor at the Moscow Conservatory. He later gave the premiere of Tchaikovsky's concerto, which had been called 'unplayable'.
ヨアヒム先生のもとで修業中です。: I am learning my craft under Professor Joachim.
ハンガリーの若い弓を、あなたの楽団に。: A young Hungarian bow, for your orchestra.
ベルリンでヨアヒムに学ぶハンガリーの若者。のちにブダペストの名教授となる。: A young Hungarian studying with Joachim in Berlin. He will become a celebrated professor in Budapest.
アウアー先生に、ずいぶん叱られました。: Professor Auer scolded me a good deal.
アウアー門下の天才少年。1905年、14歳でロンドン・デビューを果たした。「エル: A boy genius from Auer's class. He made his London debut in 1905 at 14. Known for the sweet sound called the 'Elman tone'.
アウアー先生の教室は、天才ばかりで大変です。: Professor Auer's class is hard going — all geniuses.
あなたの楽団で、腕を試させてください。: Let me try my hand in your orchestra.
ペテルブルク音楽院でアウアーに学ぶ若者。のちにアメリカで名教師となった。: A young man studying with Auer at the St Petersburg Conservatory. He later became a famous teacher in America.
14歳のとき、ブラームスさんの前で協奏曲を弾きました。: At 14 I played the concerto before Herr Brahms.
ポーランドの魂の音を、あなたの楽団に。: The sound of the Polish soul, for your orchestra.
ポーランド出身の天才。1896年、13歳でブラームスの前で協奏曲を弾き、作曲者を: A Polish-born genius. In 1896, aged 13, he played the concerto before Brahms and is said to have moved the composer to tears.
まだ12歳ですけど、子ども扱いしないでください。: I am only twelve, but please do not treat me as a child.
フバイ門下の神童。1903年、10歳でベルリンにデビューし、翌年ロンドンでも評判: A prodigy from Hubay's class. He made his Berlin debut in 1903 at the age of 10 and won acclaim in London the next year. Sibelius dedicated his concerto to him.
新大陸の弓を、あなたの楽団に。: The bow of the New World, for your orchestra.
アメリカの名ヴァイオリニスト。ヨアヒムに学び、チャイコフスキーやシベリウスの協奏: A leading American violinist. She studied with Joachim and gave the American premieres of the Tchaikovsky and Sibelius concertos.

ヨアヒム四重奏団の第2ヴァイオリンです。: I am second violin of the Joachim Quartet.
ベルリンの確かな弓を、あなたの楽団に。: The sure bow of Berlin, for your orchestra.
ボヘミア出身でヨアヒムの右腕。1905年、R.シュトラウスの指揮でシベリウスの協: Born in Bohemia, Joachim's right hand. In 1905 he gave the premiere of the revised Sibelius concerto under R. Strauss.
パガニーニの全曲を、一晩で弾きましたよ。: I have played all of Paganini in a single evening.
ドイツの技巧派。シベリウスの協奏曲を初演するはずだったが、日程の都合で機会を逃し: A German virtuoso. He was to have given the premiere of Sibelius's concerto but missed the chance over scheduling.
街角で弾いていたこともあるんです。: I once played on street corners.
あなたの楽団で、もう一度夢を。: In your orchestra, let me dream once more.
イギリスの女性ヴァイオリニスト。貧しい家に生まれ路上でも弾いたが、才能を見出され: An English woman violinist. Born poor, she played in the streets, but her talent was discovered and she reached the first rank.
ウィーン・フィルのコンマスを、もう二十数年やっています。: I have been concertmaster of the Vienna Philharmonic for twenty-odd years.
ウィーンの音を、あなたの楽団に。: The sound of Vienna, for your orchestra.
ウィーン・フィルの名コンサートマスターで、マーラーの妹の夫。ロゼー四重奏団を率い: Celebrated concertmaster of the Vienna Philharmonic and husband of Mahler's sister. He led the Rosé Quartet.

リュートの最後の巨匠、などと呼ばれております。: They call me the last great master of the lute, and such things.

この高音は、わたしにしか吹けませんよ。: No one but I can play these high notes.
あなたの楽団の祝祭に、トランペットを。: A trumpet for your orchestra's festivities.
ライプツィヒの町楽師長で、バッハのカンタータの高いトランペットを吹いた。肖像画に: Senior town musician of Leipzig, who played the high trumpet parts in Bach's cantatas. His portrait shows him holding a coiled trumpet.
ナポリの人は、わたしをフランチェスキエッロと呼びます。: In Naples they call me Francischello.
チェロの歌を、あなたの楽団に。: The song of the cello, for your orchestra.
ナポリの名チェリスト。A.スカルラッティは彼と共演して「人の姿をした天使でなけれ: A celebrated cellist of Naples. According to Geminiani, A. Scarlatti said after playing with him that 'only an angel in human form could play like that'.
スペインの宮廷で、静かに暮らしています。: I live quietly at the Spanish court.
チェロと弦楽五重奏の響きを、あなたの楽団に。: The sound of the cello and the string quintet, for your orchestra.
チェロの名手で作曲家。スペインの王族に仕えながら、パリで数多くの作品を出版した。: A cello virtuoso and composer. While serving Spanish royalty he published a great many works in Paris. The famous 'Minuet' is a movement of a string quintet.
ハイドン楽長のもとで、もう何年も弾いています。: I have played under Kapellmeister Haydn for years now.
エステルハージ家の低音を、あなたの楽団に。: The bass of the Esterházys, for your orchestra.
エステルハージ家の首席チェリスト。ハイドンのチェロ協奏曲ニ長調は彼のために書かれ: Principal cellist to the Esterházy family. Haydn's Cello Concerto in D was written for him.
ヴィオラにも、独奏の喜びがあるのです。: The viola, too, knows the joy of the solo.
あなたの楽団に、ヴィオラの声を。: The voice of the viola, for your orchestra.
マンハイム楽派の大家の息子で、ヴィオラとヴィオラ・ダモーレの名手。ヴィオラ協奏曲: Son of the great master of the Mannheim school and a virtuoso of the viola and viola d'amore. His viola concerto is still an audition standard.
本名はヤン・ヴァーツラフ・スティフ。逃亡中の身でしてね。: My real name is Jan Václav Stich. I am a fugitive, you see.
ホルンの奇跡を、あなたの楽団に。: The miracle of the horn, for your orchestra.
ボヘミア出身のホルンの大名手。主人の伯爵のもとから逃げ出して名を変えた。のちにベ: A great horn virtuoso from Bohemia. He ran away from the count he served and changed his name. Beethoven later wrote a horn sonata for him.
モーツァルト君は、楽譜にわたしの悪口を書くんですよ。: Young Mozart writes rude remarks about me in the score.
チーズ屋の片手間ですが、ホルンなら任せてください。: It is a sideline to the cheese shop, but for the horn you can count on me.
モーツァルトのホルン協奏曲を吹いた友人。モーツァルトは楽譜に「ロバのロイトゲープ: The friend who played Mozart's horn concertos. Mozart scribbled jokes in the score such as 'Leutgeb the ass'.
オーボエは、人の声にいちばん近い楽器です。: The oboe is the instrument closest to the human voice.
マンハイムのオーボエを、あなたの楽団に。: The Mannheim oboe, for your orchestra.
マンハイム楽派のオーボエの名手。モーツァルトは彼のためにオーボエ四重奏曲を書いた: An oboe virtuoso of the Mannheim school. Mozart wrote his Oboe Quartet for him.
ハープの改良にも、取り組んでおります。: I am also at work on improving the harp.
ハープの調べを、あなたの楽団に。: The strains of the harp, for your orchestra.
ボヘミア出身のハープの名手。パリで楽器の改良にも取り組み、ハープ音楽を大きく広げ: A harp virtuoso from Bohemia. In Paris he also worked on improving the instrument and greatly widened the harp's music.
目は見えませんが、音はすべて見えています。: I cannot see, but I see every note.
あなたの楽団で、弾かせてください。: Let me play in your orchestra.
幼くして視力を失ったウィーンのピアニスト・歌手。モーツァルトやサリエリと親しく、: A Viennese pianist and singer who lost her sight in early childhood. A friend of Mozart and Salieri, she later devoted herself to musical education for the blind.
チェロにエンドピンをつけたら、ずっと楽になりました。: Since I fitted an endpin to the cello, everything has been easier.
チェロのパガニーニを、あなたの楽団に。: The Paganini of the cello, for your orchestra.
「チェロのパガニーニ」と呼ばれたベルギーの名手。チェロを床に立てるエンドピンを広: A Belgian virtuoso called 'the Paganini of the cello'. He is credited with popularising the endpin that rests the cello on the floor.
練習曲なら、まだまだ書きますよ。: Études? I have plenty more to write.
ドレスデンの低音を、あなたの楽団に。: The bass of Dresden, for your orchestra.
ドレスデン宮廷の首席チェリスト。彼の練習曲は、今もチェロ学習者が必ず通る道。: Principal cellist of the Dresden court. His études are still a road every cello student must travel.
教会のオルガンも弾いています。: I play the organ in church as well.
ヴィオラの憂愁を、あなたの楽団に。: The melancholy of the viola, for your orchestra.
パリのヴィオラ奏者・オルガン奏者。ベルリオーズの『イタリアのハロルド』の独奏を初: A violist and organist of Paris. He gave the first performance of the solo part in Berlioz's Harold en Italie. A devout man, he is said to have played at the Opéra with his back turned so as not to see the stage.
ショパン君に、3年みっちり教えて差し上げると申し出たのですがね。: I offered to give young Chopin three thorough years of lessons, you know.
パリ随一のピアノを、あなたの楽団に。: The foremost piano in Paris, for your orchestra.
パリのピアノ界の大御所で、プレイエル社の共同経営者。ショパンに3年間の弟子入りを: The grand old man of the piano in Paris and a partner in the firm of Pleyel. He urged Chopin to study with him for three years and was refused.
ベルリオーズさんとの婚約は、もう昔の話です。: My engagement to Monsieur Berlioz is ancient history.
あなたの楽団で、華やかに弾きましょう。: In your orchestra I shall play brilliantly.
パリの名女性ピアニスト。ベルリオーズの婚約者だったがピアノ製造業者プレイエルと結: A celebrated woman pianist of Paris. She was engaged to Berlioz but married the piano maker Pleyel, to Berlioz's fury.
ショパンもリストも、わたしの友人です。: Chopin and Liszt are both my friends.
パリの人脈ごと、あなたの楽団に。: My Paris connections and all, for your orchestra.
パリで活躍したドイツ人ピアニスト。ショパン、リスト、メンデルスゾーンの共通の友人: A German pianist active in Paris. A friend in common of Chopin, Liszt and Mendelssohn.
ハープでも、オーケストラのような音が出せますよ。: Even a harp can sound like an orchestra.
ハープの革命を、あなたの楽団に。: A revolution on the harp, for your orchestra.
「ハープのリスト」と呼ばれたイギリスの名手。ベルリオーズが絶賛した。: An English virtuoso called 'the Liszt of the harp'. Berlioz praised him to the skies.

ギターは小さなオーケストラです。: The guitar is a small orchestra.
スペインのギターを、あなたの楽団に。: The Spanish guitar, for your orchestra.
スペインのギターの巨匠。パリとロンドンで活躍し、「ギターのベートーヴェン」と呼ば: The great master of the Spanish guitar. Active in Paris and London, he was called 'the Beethoven of the guitar'.
ベーム式？ わたしは昔ながらのフルートで十分です。: The Boehm system? The old flute is quite enough for me.
パリのフルートを、あなたの楽団に。: The flute of Paris, for your orchestra.
パリ・オペラ座とパリ音楽院のフルートの重鎮。新しいベーム式フルートには最後まで反: The leading flautist of the Paris Opéra and Conservatoire. He opposed the new Boehm flute to the last.
妻はリストの愛弟子、ゾフィー・メンターです。: My wife is Liszt's favourite pupil, Sophie Menter.
チェロの華やかさを、あなたの楽団に。: The brilliance of the cello, for your orchestra.
プラハ出身の名チェリスト。ウィーン宮廷歌劇場の首席を務め、のちにブダペスト音楽院: A celebrated cellist from Prague. Principal at the Vienna Court Opera, later professor at the Budapest Academy.
ロンドンの「月曜ポピュラー・コンサート」の常連です。: I am a regular at London's Monday Popular Concerts.
ロンドン随一のチェロを、あなたの楽団に。: The foremost cello in London, for your orchestra.
イタリア出身でロンドンを拠点にした大チェリスト。1844年、借り物の楽器で弾く彼: A great cellist, born in Italy and based in London. In 1844 Liszt, impressed that he was playing on a borrowed instrument, gave him an Amati cello.
ヨアヒム四重奏団のチェロです。: I am the cellist of the Joachim Quartet.
ベルリンの低音を、あなたの楽団に。: The bass of Berlin, for your orchestra.
ヨアヒム四重奏団のチェリスト。のちにブラームスの二重協奏曲をヨアヒムと初演した。: Cellist of the Joachim Quartet. He later gave the premiere of Brahms's Double Concerto with Joachim.
チャイコフスキー『ロココ風の主題による変奏曲』: Tchaikovsky: Variations on a Rococo Theme
チャイコフスキー君の楽譜、少し手を入れておきましたよ。: I have touched up young Tchaikovsky's score a little.
モスクワ音楽院のチェロを、あなたの楽団に。: The cello of the Moscow Conservatory, for your orchestra.
モスクワ音楽院のチェロ教授。チャイコフスキーの『ロココ風の主題による変奏曲』を初: Professor of cello at the Moscow Conservatory. He gave the premiere of Tchaikovsky's Rococo Variations, but angered the composer by reordering them on his own authority.
リスト先生には、わたしが一番の弟子だと言われました。: Maestro Liszt told me I was his finest pupil.
あなたの楽団で、リスト仕込みの技を。: Art schooled by Liszt, in your orchestra.
リストが「唯一の娘」と呼んだ愛弟子で、当時最高の女性ピアニストのひとり。夫はチェ: The favourite pupil Liszt called his 'only daughter', one of the finest women pianists of her day. Her husband was the cellist Popper.
名教師の耳を、あなたの楽団に。: A great teacher's ear, for your orchestra.
ツェルニーに学んだ名教師。のちにウィーンでパデレフスキやシュナーベルを育てた。: A great teacher who had studied with Czerny. In Vienna he later trained Paderewski and Schnabel.
8歳のとき、リンカーン大統領の前で弾きました。: At the age of eight I played before President Lincoln.
ベネズエラの情熱を、あなたの楽団に。: The passion of Venezuela, for your orchestra.
ベネズエラ出身の女性ピアニスト。少女時代にホワイトハウスでリンカーンの前で弾いた: A woman pianist from Venezuela. As a girl she played for Lincoln at the White House. She was called 'the Valkyrie of the piano'.

ワーグナーの音楽は嫌いです。吹けばうまいがね。: I dislike Wagner's music. Though I play it well enough.
あなたの楽団に、ドイツ一のホルンを。: The finest horn in Germany, for your orchestra.
ミュンヘン宮廷楽団の首席ホルン奏者で、R.シュトラウスの父。ワーグナー嫌いで知ら: Principal horn of the Munich court orchestra and father of R. Strauss. Famous for detesting Wagner, though the composer himself acknowledged his playing.
ブダペストで若い人たちを教えています。: I teach young people in Budapest.
名教授のチェロを、あなたの楽団に。: A great professor's cello, for your orchestra.
ブダペスト音楽院の名教授。彼の練習曲集は、今もチェリストの必修。: A celebrated professor at the Budapest Academy. His études are still required study for cellists.
ゲヴァントハウスで、もう30年以上弾いています。: I have played at the Gewandhaus for more than 30 years.
ライプツィヒの伝統を、あなたの楽団に。: The tradition of Leipzig, for your orchestra.
ゲヴァントハウス管弦楽団の首席チェリストで名教師。のちにフォイアマンやピアティゴ: Principal cellist of the Gewandhaus Orchestra and a great teacher. He later trained Feuermann and Piatigorsky.
カザルスさんとは……いろいろありまして。: With Señor Casals… a good deal has happened.
ポルトガルの情熱を、あなたの楽団に。: The passion of Portugal, for your orchestra.
ポルトガルの女性チェリスト。カザルスの恋人として知られ、のちに英国で大人気となっ: A Portuguese woman cellist. Known as Casals's companion, she later became enormously popular in Britain.
ヴィオラを、ヴァイオリンの落ちこぼれの楽器とは言わせません。: I will not have the viola called the instrument of failed violinists.
ヴィオラの独奏を、あなたの楽団で。: The solo viola, in your orchestra.
ヴィオラを独奏楽器に押し上げた先駆者。彼のために多くの作曲家がヴィオラ曲を書いた: The pioneer who raised the viola to a solo instrument. Many composers wrote viola works for him.
チェコ四重奏団でヴィオラを弾いています。: I play the viola in the Czech Quartet.
ボヘミアの内声を、あなたの楽団に。: The inner voices of Bohemia, for your orchestra.
チェコ四重奏団のヴィオラ奏者で、ドヴォルザークの弟子。のちに作曲家・指揮者として: Violist of the Czech Quartet and a pupil of Dvořák. He was later active as a composer and conductor.
結婚は4回しましたけど、ピアノは一筋です。: I have married four times, but to the piano I have been faithful.
ピアノのワルキューレを、あなたの楽団に。: The Valkyrie of the piano, for your orchestra.
「ピアノのワルキューレ」と呼ばれた大ピアニスト。ベルリンに住み、マクダウェルら多: A great pianist called 'the Valkyrie of the piano'. She lived in Berlin and trained many pupils, MacDowell among them.
リスト先生の最後の世代の弟子です。: I am of Maestro Liszt's last generation of pupils.
リスト直伝の技を、あなたの楽団に。: Art straight from Liszt, for your orchestra.
リスト晩年の弟子。長く第一線で弾き続けた大ピアニスト。: A pupil of Liszt's last years. A great pianist who went on playing at the highest level for a long time.
左手だけで、ショパンの練習曲を弾いてみせましょう。: I shall play you a Chopin étude with the left hand alone.
ピアニストのためのピアニストを、あなたの楽団に。: The pianist's pianist, for your orchestra.
「ピアニストのためのピアニスト」と呼ばれた超絶技巧家。ショパンの練習曲をさらに難: A transcendent technician called 'the pianist's pianist'. He arranged Chopin's études to make them harder still.
皮肉なら、ピアノと同じくらい得意ですよ。: I am as good at sarcasm as I am at the piano.
リスト門下の超絶技巧家。毒舌でも有名だった。: A transcendent technician of Liszt's school. Equally famous for his sharp tongue.
妻のロジーナも、ピアニストです。: My wife Rosina is a pianist too.
モスクワのピアノを、あなたの楽団に。: The piano of Moscow, for your orchestra.
1895年のルビンシテイン・コンクールの覇者。のちに妻ロジーナとともにジュリアー: Winner of the 1895 Rubinstein Competition. He later taught at the Juilliard School with his wife Rosina.
ラヴェル君とは、子どものころからの友達です。: Ravel and I have been friends since we were children.
新しい音楽を、あなたの楽団で初演しましょう。: Let us premiere new music with your orchestra.
スペイン出身のピアニスト。ラヴェルやドビュッシーの作品を次々と初演した。: A pianist from Spain. He gave the first performances of one work after another by Ravel and Debussy.
演奏より良い音楽を、弾きたいのです。: I want to play music that is better than it can be played.
レシェティツキ門下。のちにベートーヴェンのピアノ・ソナタ全曲を初めて録音した。: A pupil of Leschetizky. He later made the first recording of all Beethoven's piano sonatas.
ハープのための曲がないなら、自分で書きます。: If there is no music for the harp, I write it myself.
あなたの楽団に、ハープの響きを。: The sound of the harp, for your orchestra.
フランスのハープの名手。自作のハープ協奏曲で、ハープの可能性を大きく広げた。: A French harp virtuoso. Her own harp concerto greatly widened the possibilities of the instrument.
ドビュッシー『牧神の午後への前奏曲』: Debussy: Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune
ニューヨークに着いたばかりです。: I have only just arrived in New York.
フランスのフルートを、新大陸と、あなたの楽団に。: The French flute, for the New World and for your orchestra.
フランスのフルートの名手。ドビュッシーの『牧神の午後への前奏曲』の初演で吹き、1: A French flute virtuoso. He played in the premiere of Debussy's Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune and crossed to New York in 1905.
バッハの本を書き上げたところです。これから医学を学びます。: I have just finished my book on Bach. Now I shall study medicine.
オルガン奏者で神学者。1905年にバッハ論を出版し、同じ年に医師をめざして医学を: Organist and theologian. In 1905 he published his study of Bach and the same year began studying medicine to become a doctor. He later devoted himself to medical work in Africa.
名チェリスト、フランチェスキエッロことアルボレアが世を去った。: The great cellist Alborea, known as Francischello, has died.
ホルンの名手プントがプラハで世を去った。: The horn virtuoso Punto has died in Prague.

クレモナの工房で、老ストラディヴァリがいまも新作を仕上げている。当時はまだ「現役: In his Cremona workshop the aged Stradivari is still finishing new instruments. In those days it was simply 'an instrument by a living master'.
タルティーニが弾き、その弟子筋を経てリピンスキの手に渡ったと伝わる名器。: A great instrument said to have been played by Tartini and to have passed through his pupils into Lipiński's hands.
近代ヴァイオリン奏法の父ヴィオッティが愛した一挺。: The violin beloved of Viotti, father of modern violin playing.
イルカのように輝くニスから名づけられた。のちにハイフェッツが愛用した。: Named for varnish that shimmers like a dolphin. Heifetz later played it.
サラサーテが遺言でパリ音楽院に遺した。いまもパリの楽器博物館にある。: Left by Sarasate in his will to the Paris Conservatoire. It is still in the instrument museum in Paris.
フーベルマンの愛器。のちに二度盗まれ、半世紀ものあいだ行方不明になった。: Huberman's instrument. It was later stolen twice and was missing for half a century.
R.クロイツェルが弾いたと伝わる晩年のストラディヴァリ。: A late Stradivari said to have been played by R. Kreutzer.
ほとんど弾かれず、作られたときの姿をとどめる一挺。: Scarcely played, it remains as it was when made.
ヴュータンが愛した、デル・ジェズ最高傑作のひとつ。: Beloved of Vieuxtemps; among the supreme masterpieces of del Gesù.
イザイの愛器。のちにアイザック・スターンが弾いた。: Ysaÿe's instrument. Later played by Isaac Stern.
デル・ジェズ最晩年の一挺。: An instrument from del Gesù's very last years.
クライスラーが弾き、のちにアメリカ議会図書館に寄贈した。: Played by Kreisler, who later gave it to the Library of Congress.
ストラディヴァリの工房に近いところで腕を磨いたクレモナの名工。: A master of Cremona who learned his craft close to the Stradivari workshop.
各地を渡り歩いた名工。力強い音で人気が高い。: A master who moved from city to city. Much prized for his powerful sound.
ブレシア派の祖の作。オーレ・ブルが彫刻入りの一挺を愛用した。: By the founder of the Brescian school. Ole Bull played a carved example.

ナポレオンが試しに弾こうとして、靴の拍車で傷をつけたと伝わる。: Napoleon is said to have tried it and scratched it with the spur of his boot.
「ヴェネツィアの獅子」と呼ばれた名工。太く豊かな音。: The maker called 'the Lion of Venice'. A broad, rich sound.

どの時代にもなぜか現れる、雷鳴のようなティンパニ奏者。ピアニッシモという言葉を知: A timpanist like a thunderclap, who somehow appears in every era. The word pianissimo is unknown to him. A tower of strength at a symphony's climax, but in quiet music he drowns everything.
ティンパニ（第3楽章から終楽章へ）: Timpani (from the third movement into the finale)
オーボエ（第2楽章の歌）: Oboe (the song of the second movement)

ドビュッシー『神聖な舞曲と世俗的な舞曲』（1904）: Debussy: Danse sacrée et danse profane (1904)
ハープ奏者パウエルが弾くために書かれた: written for the harpist Powell to play
マンハイムのラムが何度も吹いて評判をとった: Ramm of Mannheim played it many times to acclaim
ヴェネツィアのオーボエ協奏曲。のちにバッハが鍵盤用に編曲した: a Venetian oboe concerto, later arranged for keyboard by Bach
ドンナー親方の一撃で、山場が雷のように決まる（+1.2）: Meister Donner's stroke lands the climax like thunder (+1.2)
ドンナー親方の太鼓が、ほかの音をすべてかき消した（-1.3）: Meister Donner's drums drowned every other sound (-1.3)
ピアニッシモの箇所で{n}が全力で叩いた。客席の紳士が椅子から落ちた。: In a pianissimo passage {n} struck with full force. A gentleman in the stalls fell off his chair.
{n}がバチを一本、客席に飛ばした。拾った子どもが記念に持ち帰った。: {n} sent a drumstick flying into the audience. The child who picked it up took it home as a souvenir.
雷鳴の一撃！ 聴衆が飛び上がった: A stroke of thunder! The audience jumped
キーが2つか3つしかない、初期のオーボエ。: An early oboe with only two or three keys.
パリのトリエベール工房のオーボエ。キーの仕組みを次々に改良した名工房。: An oboe from the Triebert workshop in Paris, which improved the keywork again and again.
ジレとロレーが仕上げた「音楽院式」オーボエ。今のオーボエの原型。: The 'Conservatoire system' oboe perfected by Gillet and Lorée: the prototype of today's oboe.
ペダルを一段だけ踏み込める、昔のハープ。: The older harp, whose pedals move one step only.
1810年ごろセバスチャン・エラールが特許をとったハープ。どの調でも弾ける。: The harp Sébastien Érard patented about 1810. It can play in any key.
ハンドル一つで音程を変えられるティンパニ。ライプツィヒで改良が進んだ。: Timpani whose pitch changes with a single handle. Much improved in Leipzig.

声部は、いくつでも重ねてみせましょう。: I shall stack as many voices as you please.
国王陛下も、思わずご起立なさいますぞ。: Even His Majesty will find himself rising.
曲なら、いまここで書きましょう。: A piece? I shall write one here and now.
夢で悪魔が弾いた音を、いま再現しよう。: The notes the Devil played in my dream — I shall reproduce them now.
王を癒やす声: The voice that heals a king
この一声で、王の憂いを晴らします。: With one note I lift the King's melancholy.
右手と左手、どちらが上か当ててごらんなさい。: Right hand or left: guess which is on top.
和声こそ、音楽の根本原理です。: Harmony is the fundamental principle of music.
天使のように、弾いてみせましょう。: I shall play it like an angel.
悪魔のように弾くのが、わたしの流儀。: To play like a devil is my way.
この迷宮、抜けられますかな。: Can you find your way out of this labyrinth?
格子の向こうから、天上の音を。: From behind the grille, the sound of heaven.
陛下のためだけに、三百曲書きました。: For His Majesty alone I wrote three hundred pieces.
この高音、どなたにも真似できませんわ。: No one can imitate this high note.
頭の中では、もう全部できあがっています。: In my head it is all finished already.
居眠りしている方、お目覚めの時間ですよ。: Those dozing: it is time to wake up.
心が鳴らす音を、聴いてくれ。: Hear the sound the heart makes.
剣も弓も、わたしの手の中で舞う。: Sword or bow, each dances in my hand.
静かな音ほど、遠くまで届くのです。: The quieter the sound, the farther it carries.
音楽は、詩に仕えるものです。: Music is the servant of poetry.
さあ、ご婦人がた。お気を確かに。: Now, ladies — do keep hold of yourselves.
ピアノに、歌わせてみせます。: I shall make the piano sing.
オーケストラが、あと五百人ほど要るのです。: I need about five hundred more in the orchestra.
だんだん大きく、だんだん楽しく！: Louder and louder, merrier and merrier!
命を燃やす歌: A song that burns life away
歌うときは、いつも最後のつもりで。: When I sing, I sing as if it were the last time.
さあ、踊らずにはいられないでしょう。: Come — you cannot help but dance.
手が三本あるように、聴こえるでしょう。: It sounds as though I had three hands, does it not?
フィヨルドの風を、弓に乗せて。: The wind of the fjords, on my bow.
低音が鳴れば、劇場が揺れます。: When the bass sounds, the theatre shakes.
パガニーニ先生の後ろで、盗み聴きしましたよ。: I eavesdropped from behind Maestro Paganini.
巨人の足音が聞こえる。それでも書く。: I hear the tread of a giant. Still I write.
楽譜に書かれたことを、まっすぐに。: What is written in the score, played straight.
指が、勝手に踊り出すのです。: My fingers begin to dance of themselves.
この旋律で、泣かない人はいません。: No one hears this melody without weeping.
いまは、祈るように弾くのです。: Now I play as one prays.
出演料は、金貨で前払いですのよ。: My fee is paid in advance, in gold.
これは、内緒の冗談ですよ。: This is a private joke, you understand.
ウィーンの夜は、ワルツで更けるのです。: Vienna's nights grow late to the waltz.
この弓は、稲妻よりも速い。: This bow is quicker than lightning.
聴衆が騒ぐなら、もう一度最初からだ。: If the audience makes a noise, we start again from the beginning.
世界を抱く交響曲: A symphony that embraces the world
交響曲とは、世界をまるごと作ることだ。: A symphony must be like the world: it must contain everything.
古い名曲を見つけましてね（作ったのはわたしです）。: I found an old masterpiece, you see (I wrote it).
笑え道化師。たとえ心が泣いていても。: Laugh, clown — though your heart is weeping.
毎朝、まずバッハを弾くのです。: Every morning, first of all, I play Bach.
客席が騒ぐ？ それは成功の証です。: The house in uproar? That is the proof of success.
この手なら、鍵盤の端から端まで届きます。: With these hands I reach from one end of the keyboard to the other.
一挺のヴァイオリンで、オーケストラを鳴らそう。: With one violin I shall make an orchestra sound.
どうぞ、聴かなくて結構です。: Please, there is no need to listen.
目で振れば、棒はいらない。: Conduct with the eyes and you need no baton.
この声で、皇帝の苦悩を。: With this voice, the Tsar's torment.
弦の上を、水が流れるように。: Like water running over the strings.
ハープにも、独奏の大曲を。: Great solo works for the harp, too.
音程の変わる雷を、お聴かせしよう。: Let me play you thunder that changes its pitch.
弟子たちが、世界中で同じ音を吹いています。: My pupils play the same sound all over the world.
ワシの若いころはなあ……今夜は本気じゃ。: When I was young, mind you… Tonight I mean it.
客席で失神者が続出！: Swoon after swoon in the audience!
ブチッ！ 弦が切れた……それでも弾き続ける！: Snap! A string has gone… and still the playing goes on!
ウィーンの宮廷楽長は、このわたしだ。: The court Kapellmeister of Vienna is I.
宮廷楽長の威光: The majesty of the court Kapellmeister
皇帝陛下のお気に入りは、どちらかな？: Which of us, I wonder, is His Majesty's favourite?
……見事だ。弟子にしたいほどだよ。: …Splendid. I could wish you were my pupil.
宮廷の作法を、もう少し学んでから来たまえ。: Learn a little more of the manners of the court, and come back.
鍵盤の上なら、誰にも負けん。: At the keyboard I lose to no one.
この練習曲を、弾き切れるかね？: Can you play this étude through to the end?
負けたついでだ、うちの工房のピアノを一台どうだね。: Since I have lost — how about a piano from my workshop?
指の訓練が足りん。百回さらいなさい。: Your fingers want training. Practise it a hundred times.
ライプツィヒの音楽を、お聴かせしましょう。: Let me play you the music of Leipzig.
素晴らしい。ゲヴァントハウスに招かせてください。: Wonderful. Allow me to invite you to the Gewandhaus.
バッハを、もう一度よく聴いてごらんなさい。: Listen carefully to Bach once more.
三本の手の秘密、見破れますか。: Can you see through the secret of the three hands?
リスト君にも、同じように負けましたよ。: I lost to young Liszt in just the same way.
紳士は、鍵盤を叩いたりしないものです。: A gentleman does not thump the keyboard.
悪魔に魂を売った男と、弾き比べるかね。: Will you match yourself against a man who sold his soul to the Devil?
……ふむ。悪魔も、たまには負ける。: …Hm. Even the Devil loses now and then.
今夜の入場料は、倍にさせてもらうよ。: Tonight's ticket prices will be doubled.
未来の音楽を、聴かせてやろう。: I shall let you hear the music of the future.
バイロイトで、もう一度勝負だ。: We shall settle it again in Bayreuth.
過去の音楽に、用はない。: I have no use for the music of the past.
……わたしは、話すより書くほうが得意でね。: …I am better at writing than at speaking.
いい音楽だった。ビールでもどうだ。: That was good music. A beer, perhaps?
ここにまだ怒らせていない人がいたら、失礼。: If there is anyone here I have not yet offended, I apologise.
イタリアの心を、歌で示そう。: Let me show the heart of Italy in song.
わたしは農夫だ。畑から出直そう。: I am a farmer. I shall begin again from the fields.
ブラーヴォは、イタリアの言葉だよ。: Bravo is an Italian word, you know.
赤毛の司祭のヴァイオリン、とくとお聴きあれ。: The Red Priest's violin — listen well.
ミサを抜け出してきた甲斐が……なかった。: So much for slipping out of Mass… it was not worth it.
ピエタの娘たちのほうが、まだ上手ですな。: The girls of the Pietà play better than that.
ロンドンの劇場は、わたしの庭だ。: The theatres of London are my garden.
ライプツィヒのカントルに、一度会ってみたいものだ。: I should like to meet the Kantor of Leipzig some day.
オペラの客は、正直なのだよ。: An opera audience is an honest one.
ロンドンは、わたしの旋律を待っている。: London is waiting for my melodies.
この旋律に、ロンドン中が酔いしれる。: All London is drunk on this melody.
ヘンデルと比べられるのには、もう慣れっこだ。: I am quite used to being compared with Handel.
わたしの時代は、まだ来ていないだけだ。: It is only that my time has not yet come.
もう一度、最初の小節から。: Once more, from the first bar.
英雄の生涯を、お見せしよう。: Let me show you a hero's life.
次の作品で、取り返すとしよう。: I shall make it up with the next work.
さて、印税の計算をしてこよう。: Well, I must go and work out the royalties.
規則？ それは、わたしの楽しみのためにある。: Rules? They exist for my pleasure.
このトリル、弾けるものなら弾いてみよ。: This trill — play it if you can.
ちっ……夢から覚めたか。: Tch… so you have woken from the dream.
